messages:
marco: Heads-up — StellarHealth POC kicks off Mon. They want Redwood in their VPC with a Dedicated pool behind Private connectivity. Need a concise network + auth checklist we can hand to their infra team. PrivateLink vs peering? can we use hosted API keys for the POC?

sasha: Short answer: both are possible, but PrivateLink (Interface VPCE) is usually the lowest-friction cross-account option. VPC peering works if they want full L3 routing between our dedicated subnet and theirs, but it requires more route table and CIDR coordination.

marco: Got it. What specifically do we need from them for PrivateLink?

julia: For AWS Interface endpoint (PrivateLink) we'll need: 
- List of 2-3 subnets (one per AZ preferred) for the ENIs
- Security group to attach to the endpoint (we'll ask them to allow outbound 443 to our hosted ENIs)
- Customer CIDR blocks that should be allowed to talk to the endpoint (for SG + NACL review)
- If they want private DNS, they must enable "private DNS" on the endpoint and we provide the target DNS name.

julia: Minimal SG rules (example):
- inbound: allow TCP 443 from customer CIDRs (or specific app CIDRs)
- outbound: allow 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (for TLS to control plane if needed)

julia: Also: ensure their NACLs are not blocking ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for ENI responses.\n
marco: Thanks. Hosted API keys — any caveats?

sasha: If you use Redwood hosted control plane + PrivateLink to our API, they can call our hosted service over the interface endpoint and use normal API keys.
- If they opt for a full Private deployment (customer-managed control plane or on-prem), API keys will be issued/managed inside their deployment (we don't reuse hosted keys).

sasha: TL;DR: Hosted API keys OK over PrivateLink; not applicable for a customer-local Private install.

ryan: Pricing note: for a 30-day Dedicated POC we can offer the POC pool at 50% off list, subject to a short SOW. Private installs have a minimum commit; if they want on-prem we need procurement sign-off.

marco: Perfect — do we have a config example I can forward to their infra?

julia: Paste the minimal Terraform snippet we usually share:

```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_api" {
  service_name      = "com.redwood.api"
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [var.endpoint_sg]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}
```

julia: And example SG (high-level):
```
# allow customers to call our endpoint
ingress {
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["10.10.0.0/16"]
}
```

julia: Connectivity test (from their bastion):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health
# expect 200 and json {"status":"ok"}
```

marco: Nice. Anything specific for the Dedicated pool itself? Subnet / routing notes for the GPU instances?

julia: Dedicated pools run in our account (or in their account for Private) depending on the deployment mode. For hosted Dedicated (our account) with PrivateLink: no routing changes needed on their compute side beyond allowing access to the Interface endpoint. If Dedicated is provisioned into their account (customer-managed infra):
- Provide 3 private subnets (AZ-aware) with at least /24 each recommended for scaling and ENIs
- Route tables: NAT gateway or egress path for images/patching, or explicit egress to our artifact mirrors if locked down
- Security groups: allow outbound to our model registry endpoints and container registries (we'll share CIDRs/hostnames)

marco: They're strict on egress — security team will only allow connections to a few FQDNs.

sasha: We can provide a short allowlist: 
- api.redwoodcloud.com (TLS 443)
- artifacts.redwoodcloud.com (443)
- model-cdn.redwoodcloud.com (443)
We'll also provide IP ranges for the POC. If they require FQDN-only restrictions, we recommend using a proxy that enforces TLS SNI/HTTP Host rules.

security-bot: Uploaded: SOC2 Type II summary + security questionnaire link: https://redwoodhq.example/sales/sec-qa/stellarhealth. Please complete the questionnaire sections: network diagram, data flow, and key rotation policy.

marco: I'll ping them to fill the questionnaire. Any known blockers?

julia: One common blocker: private DNS. If they enable private DNS on the VPCE, their DNS must forward the redwood domain to the endpoint. If they don't want private DNS, they'll need to add an entry in their internal DNS to point api.redwoodcloud.com -> vpce-<id>.

julia: Another blocker is overlapping CIDRs for peering. If they prefer peering, confirm there is no overlapping /16.

marco: Action items I have:
- send Terraform snippet + SG examples to Stellar infra (today)
- attach SOC2 summary + security questionnaire link (today)
- confirm which route (PrivateLink vs peering) they prefer and get subnets list (by EOD Tue)

ryan: I'll draft the POC SOW and pricing note and share in #contracts.

deploy-bot: log: vpce-attach request created by julia at 1795054360 — waiting on customer subnet IDs.

marco: Thanks team — I'll update after the infra call. :thumbsup:
